The challenge

Statements submitted for financial monitoring typically run 40-90 pages and arrive in more than ten layouts, including text PDFs, spreadsheets, scans and phone photographs. With no common structure across banks, specialists had to extract and check each document manually.

One large statement required around 11.5 hours of work. Repetitive extraction slowed review and increased the risk of human error. ASVIO Bank needed structured, traceable results that its compliance team could review efficiently.

The solution

SoftBees developed the AI agent for first-level AML review; Techlegion is the Delivery Partner of Record for the engagement. The agent reconstructs transaction tables, validates the extracted data and produces an explainable risk assessment. Findings cite the relevant transaction rows and identify what the compliance officer should verify. The final decision stays with the officer.

The team designed three processing paths, using Claude where document complexity requires it.

  1. Text PDFs: deterministic extraction

    A Java parser reads the text layer and table geometry without a model call.

  2. Text PDFs with Claude post-processing

    Claude receives the page image and extracted rows to repair split cell values, unidentified counterparty codes and truncated payment descriptions.

  3. Scans and photographs: visual extraction

    Claude reads pages directly, with one call per page in parallel. Pages can be divided into bands to retain the resolution needed to recognise digits and transaction details.

All paths normalise identifiers, verify IBAN checksums and reconcile totals against the statement. Rule-based AML analysis checks nine categories, with evidence and a next verification step for each finding. Outputs are available as JSON through an API or as XLSX.

Why Claude

SoftBees compared models on real banking documents. In the team's tests, local open-source models without fine-tuning struggled with Ukrainian banking identifiers, including MFO bank routing codes and EDRPOU company registration numbers. Claude produced the required structured results without fine-tuning, helping the team meet the implementation timeline.

The solution uses Claude 3.7 Sonnet through the Amazon Bedrock API. The application can run in the cloud or within bank infrastructure as a Docker container or Java JAR. Claude inference uses the Amazon Bedrock API.

The impact

ASVIO Bank moved from manual extraction to structured review of findings. The measured large-statement workflow fell from 11.5 hours of specialist work to approximately one hour. More than 4,000 documents were processed during 2025-2026.

The team reports automated processing times of 1-2 seconds for spreadsheets and text-layer PDFs, and 60-90 seconds for scans and photographs. These processing times are separate from the approximately one-hour specialist review workflow.

“We have effectively eliminated human error; we cut the processing time for a single document by 90%, from 11.5 hours to one hour; and we reduced the cost of processing a case of documents seventeen-fold.”
Yevhen Shulika, Chairman of the Board, ASVIO BankDIGITAL HORIZONS: SMART BANKING, September 2025. Customer statement.
